title: Per-city delivery settings
scenario: Each city has its own radius, fee and minimum order; a config typo once set the minimum order to ₹0.
stack: Spring Boot 4.1.1 · Java 25 · @ConfigurationProperties records · @Validated · profiles · relaxed binding · @AutoConfiguration · MockMvc
simulation: Delivery terms are demo values, not Basketo's. A delivery check only answers whether an order could be delivered; no order is placed. Distances are straight-line, computed on the server.

Level 1, about 5 minutes. Plain language: no code.

The problem in real life

  1. A config change goes out

    Someone edits Pune's settings and types minimun-order-paise. The app starts, as always.

  2. Nothing fails, and that is the problem

    The real key is now missing, so the minimum order is 0. Customers in Pune order a single ₹10 lemon with free-feeling delivery, and every order loses money. Meanwhile the app also trusts the distance the phone sends.

  3. The fix

    Bind settings into a validated record that refuses unknown keys, missing values and impossible numbers at startup, and compute distance on the server from the address.

A bad setting should stop the deployment, not reach a customer.

What are we building?

GET /cities/{city}/delivery-terms shows a city's radius, fee and minimum order. POST /delivery-checks says whether an address and an order amount can be delivered, with the distance the server computed.

An everyday analogy

A restaurant's opening checklist: if the gas reading is missing or impossible, the kitchen does not open. It does not open and hope the reading was fine.

How it works in 4 steps

  1. At startup, Spring binds basketo.cities.* into records, with profile and environment overrides applied.
  2. It validates them: unknown keys, missing values, a radius over 15 km or a minimum under ₹99 stop the start, naming the property.
  3. A check arrives with coordinates; the server computes the distance from the city's store.
  4. It answers with the distance, the fee, and any reasons it cannot deliver.
Check yourself: why use Long instead of long for the minimum order?

A missing long silently becomes 0. A missing Long is null, which @NotNull refuses, so a misspelt key is caught at startup.

What this station is not

  • No road distances. Straight-line distance; a road service could replace it.
  • No live config changes. Settings are read at startup; challenge 3 discusses changes without a restart.
  • No orders. A check only.

Belongs in this tab

  • 1. Business problem
  • 2. Acceptance criteria
  • 3. Requirements

Level 2. What a teammate hands you before you build.

Business problem

Basketo (a fictional quick-commerce app) sets a delivery radius, fee and minimum order per city. A typo in a config key once set a minimum order to ₹0 and nothing failed. The delivery check also used the distance the app sent, so a modified client could get delivery anywhere.

Acceptance criteria

  1. Given a misspelt key, a missing value, a minimum below ₹99 or a radius over 15 km, then the app does not start, and the error names the property.
  2. Given an extra key nobody reads, then the app does not start.
  3. Given BASKETO_CITIES_PUNE_FEEPAISE=3000, then Pune's fee is ₹30 and its other values come from the file.
  4. Given the dev profile, then a test city exists; without it, it does not.
  5. Given an address in Koregaon Park, then 4.94 km from the Pune store, deliverable; Hinjewadi at 13.28 km with ₹99 is not, for two reasons.
  6. Given a distanceKm in the request, then 400; an unknown city, 404.

Requirements

  • Demo limits: radius 0.5 to 15 km; fee ₹0 to ₹100; minimum order at least ₹99.
  • Settings are records with wrapper types and validation; unknown keys are an error.
  • Distance is computed on the server (haversine, mean Earth radius 6,371.0088 km).
  • City names are normalised with Locale.ROOT.

Learning objectives

  • Bind configuration into records with @ConfigurationProperties.
  • Make configuration fail fast with @Validated and ignoreUnknownFields = false.
  • Use profiles and environment variable overrides.
  • Explain auto-configuration and @ConditionalOnMissingBean.
  • Compute on the server what the client could lie about.

The trap

Plausible but wrong

Unvalidated config: a typo sets the minimum order to zero and nothing fails.

The first test binds the old settings (primitives, no validation) with the typo: the app starts and Pune's minimum is 0. The second binds the real settings with the same typo: the start fails, naming cities[pune].minimumOrderPaise as null. The third shows the old check believing a client's 0 km. While building, removing @Validated turned 2 tests red, and allowing unknown keys turned 1 red.

package com.basketo.delivery;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfigurations;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.context.ConfigurationPropertiesAutoConfiguration;
import org.springframework.boot.context.properties.ConfigurationProperties;
import org.springframework.boot.context.properties.EnableConfigurationProperties;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.runner.ApplicationContextRunner;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;

import java.util.Map;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

/** The first test written for this station: it reproduces the bugs before the fix. */
class UnvalidatedConfigTrapTest {

    /** The "before" settings: primitives, no validation, unknown keys ignored. Kept only in tests. */
    @ConfigurationProperties("basketo")
    record OldSettings(Map<String, OldCity> cities) {
        record OldCity(double radiusKm, long feePaise, long minimumOrderPaise) {
        }
    }

    @Configuration
    @EnableConfigurationProperties(OldSettings.class)
    static class OldApp {
    }

    /** The "before" check: the client said how far it was. Kept only in tests. */
    static boolean oldDeliverable(double clientDistanceKm, double radiusKm) {
        return clientDistanceKm <= radiusKm;
    }

    @Test
    void theOldSettingsStartWithAMisspeltKeyAndAMinimumOfZero() {
        new ApplicationContextRunner()
                .withConfiguration(AutoConfigurations.of(ConfigurationPropertiesAutoConfiguration.class))
                .withUserConfiguration(OldApp.class)
                .withPropertyValues("basketo.cities.pune.radius-km=6.0", "basketo.cities.pune.fee-paise=2500",
                        "basketo.cities.pune.minimun-order-paise=14900")   // "minimun": one letter wrong
                .run(context -> {
                    assertThat(context).hasNotFailed();
                    assertThat(context.getBean(OldSettings.class).cities().get("pune").minimumOrderPaise()).isZero();
                });
    }

    @Test
    void theRealSettingsRefuseToStartWithThatTypo() {
        ConfigRunner.settings("basketo.cities.pune.minimun-order-paise=14900")
                // the real key is now missing: a Long, not a long, so it is null, and @NotNull stops the start
                .run(context -> assertThat(context).hasFailed().getFailure()
                        .hasStackTraceContaining("cities[pune].minimumOrderPaise").hasStackTraceContaining("rejected value [null]"));
    }

    @Test
    void theOldCheckBelievesWhateverDistanceTheClientSends() {
        assertThat(oldDeliverable(0.0, 6.0)).isTrue();   // an address 13 km away, "0 km" according to the app
    }
}

src/main/java/com/basketo/delivery/DeliveryController.java

Does
Finds the city's settings and runs the check with the server's own distance.
Why
No distance in the request at all: there is nothing for a client to lie about.
Without it
Trusting a distanceKm from the app.
package com.basketo.delivery;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.DecimalMax;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.DecimalMin;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Min;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;

@RestController
class DeliveryController {

    record Terms(String city, double radiusKm, long feePaise, long minimumOrderPaise) {
    }

    /** No distance field: the client sends where the address is; the server works out how far it is. */
    record CheckRequest(@NotBlank String city, @NotNull @DecimalMin("-90") @DecimalMax("90") Double lat,
                        @NotNull @DecimalMin("-180") @DecimalMax("180") Double lon, @NotNull @Min(1) Long orderPaise) {
    }

    record Check(String city, double distanceKm, boolean deliverable, List<String> reasons, long feePaise,
                 long minimumOrderPaise, long orderPaise) {
    }

    private final DeliverySettings settings;
    private final DistanceCalculator distance;

    DeliveryController(DeliverySettings settings, DistanceCalculator distance) {
        this.settings = settings;
        this.distance = distance;
    }

    @GetMapping("/cities/{city}/delivery-terms")
    Terms terms(@PathVariable String city) {
        String key = city.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
        DeliverySettings.City c = find(key);
        return new Terms(key, c.radiusKm(), c.feePaise(), c.minimumOrderPaise());
    }

    @PostMapping("/delivery-checks")
    Check check(@Valid @RequestBody CheckRequest r) {
        String key = r.city().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
        DeliverySettings.City c = find(key);
        double km = distance.km(c.store(), r.lat(), r.lon());
        List<String> reasons = new ArrayList<>();
        if (km > c.radiusKm()) {
            reasons.add("OUT_OF_RANGE");
        }
        if (r.orderPaise() < c.minimumOrderPaise()) {
            reasons.add("BELOW_MINIMUM");
        }
        return new Check(key, Math.round(km * 100) / 100.0, reasons.isEmpty(), reasons, c.feePaise(), c.minimumOrderPaise(), r.orderPaise());
    }

    private DeliverySettings.City find(String city) {
        DeliverySettings.City c = settings.cities().get(city);
        if (c == null) {
            ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Basketo does not deliver in this city yet.");
            p.setTitle("City not served");
            throw new ErrorResponseException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, p, null);
        }
        return c;
    }
}

src/main/java/com/basketo/delivery/DeliverySettings.java

Does
The settings as validated records.
Why
Wrapper types, constraints and ignoreUnknownFields = false: every bad setting stops the start.
Without it
The trap: primitives that default to 0, and no checks.
  • @Validated runs Bean Validation on the bound record at startup.
  • @Valid on the map values and the store location checks the nested records too.
package com.basketo.delivery;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.DecimalMax;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.DecimalMin;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Max;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Min;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotEmpty;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import org.springframework.boot.context.properties.ConfigurationProperties;
import org.springframework.validation.annotation.Validated;

import java.util.Map;

/**
 * Per-city delivery settings from configuration (basketo.cities.*), checked when the app starts. A typo in a key,
 * a missing value or a minimum order of zero stops the app from starting, instead of quietly taking orders at Rs 0.
 * Wrapper types (Long, Double), not primitives: a missing value is null and fails @NotNull, never a silent 0.
 */
@ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "basketo", ignoreUnknownFields = false)
@Validated
record DeliverySettings(@NotEmpty Map<String, @Valid @NotNull City> cities) {

    record City(@NotNull @DecimalMin("0.5") @DecimalMax("15.0") Double radiusKm,
                @NotNull @Min(0) @Max(10_000) Long feePaise,
                @NotNull @Min(value = 9_900, message = "must be at least 9900 paise (Rs 99): a demo floor") Long minimumOrderPaise,
                @NotNull @Valid Location store) {
    }

    record Location(@NotNull @DecimalMin("-90") @DecimalMax("90") Double lat, @NotNull @DecimalMin("-180") @DecimalMax("180") Double lon) {
    }
}

src/main/java/com/basketo/delivery/DistanceAutoConfiguration.java

Does
The default distance calculator, as an auto-configuration.
Why
Listed in META-INF/spring/…AutoConfiguration.imports, so it runs after the app's own beans and @ConditionalOnMissingBean can see them.
Without it
The same condition on an ordinary @Configuration: its result depends on the order definitions are processed. Spring Boot's documentation recommends the condition only on auto-configuration classes.
package com.basketo.delivery;

import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.condition.ConditionalOnMissingBean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;

/**
 * The default DistanceCalculator, declared the way Spring Boot declares its own defaults: an auto-configuration
 * (listed in META-INF/spring/...AutoConfiguration.imports). Auto-configurations run after the application's own
 * beans, so @ConditionalOnMissingBean sees them: define a DistanceCalculator yourself and this one steps aside.
 * On an ordinary @Configuration the same condition depends on scanning order, and both beans can end up created.
 */
@AutoConfiguration
public class DistanceAutoConfiguration {

    @Bean
    @ConditionalOnMissingBean
    DistanceCalculator straightLine() {
        return (from, lat, lon) -> {
            double r = 6371.0088;   // mean Earth radius, km
            double p1 = Math.toRadians(from.lat()), p2 = Math.toRadians(lat);
            double dp = p2 - p1, dl = Math.toRadians(lon - from.lon());
            double h = Math.pow(Math.sin(dp / 2), 2) + Math.cos(p1) * Math.cos(p2) * Math.pow(Math.sin(dl / 2), 2);
            return 2 * r * Math.asin(Math.sqrt(h));   // haversine: straight-line, shorter than any road
        };
    }
}

The one-method interface any distance source implements.

package com.basketo.delivery;

/** Kilometres between two points. A road-distance service could replace the default without touching callers. */
@FunctionalInterface
interface DistanceCalculator {

    double km(DeliverySettings.Location from, double lat, double lon);
}

        }
    }

    @Configuration
    @EnableConfigurationProperties(OldSettings.class)
    static class OldApp {

Startup failures, an environment variable, the dev profile, a replaced default, and a known distance.

package com.basketo.delivery;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.boot.WebApplicationType;
import org.springframework.boot.builder.SpringApplicationBuilder;
import org.springframework.context.ConfigurableApplicationContext;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.core.env.StandardEnvironment;
import org.springframework.core.env.SystemEnvironmentPropertySource;

import java.util.Map;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.within;

/** Configuration at work: validation at startup, environment variables, profiles, replaceable defaults, distance. */
class DeliveryConfigTest {

    @Test
    void invalidValuesStopTheAppStartingAndNameTheProperty() {
        ConfigRunner.settings("basketo.cities.pune.minimum-order-paise=0")
                .run(c -> assertThat(c).hasFailed().getFailure().hasStackTraceContaining("minimumOrderPaise"));
        ConfigRunner.settings("basketo.cities.pune.minimum-order-paise=14900", "basketo.cities.pune.radius-km=60")
                .run(c -> assertThat(c).hasFailed().getFailure().hasStackTraceContaining("radiusKm"));
        ConfigRunner.settings()   // minimum-order-paise missing altogether
                .run(c -> assertThat(c).hasFailed().getFailure().hasStackTraceContaining("minimumOrderPaise"));
        ConfigRunner.settings("basketo.cities.pune.minimum-order-paise=14900").run(c -> assertThat(c).hasNotFailed());
    }

    @Test
    void aMisspeltExtraKeyStopsTheAppStartingToo() {
        // every real key present, plus one nobody reads: ignoreUnknownFields = false refuses it
        ConfigRunner.settings("basketo.cities.pune.minimum-order-paise=14900", "basketo.cities.pune.feee-paise=1")
                .run(c -> assertThat(c).hasFailed().getFailure().hasStackTraceContaining("feee-paise"));
    }

    /** Starts the real app (no web server) with the given profile and pretend environment variables. */
    static ConfigurableApplicationContext app(String profile, Map<String, Object> environmentVariables) {
        StandardEnvironment env = new StandardEnvironment();
        env.getPropertySources().replace(StandardEnvironment.SYSTEM_ENVIRONMENT_PROPERTY_SOURCE_NAME,
                new SystemEnvironmentPropertySource(StandardEnvironment.SYSTEM_ENVIRONMENT_PROPERTY_SOURCE_NAME, environmentVariables));
        SpringApplicationBuilder builder = new SpringApplicationBuilder(DeliveryApplication.class).web(WebApplicationType.NONE).environment(env);
        return profile == null ? builder.run() : builder.profiles(profile).run();
    }

    @Test
    void anEnvironmentVariableOverridesOneValue() {
        try (var ctx = app(null, Map.of("BASKETO_CITIES_PUNE_FEEPAISE", "3000"))) {
            DeliverySettings s = ctx.getBean(DeliverySettings.class);
            assertThat(s.cities().get("pune").feePaise()).isEqualTo(3000);
            assertThat(s.cities().get("pune").minimumOrderPaise()).isEqualTo(14900);   // everything else from the file
        }
    }

    @Test
    void theDevProfileAddsATestCity() {
        try (var dev = app("dev", Map.of()); var normal = app(null, Map.of())) {
            assertThat(dev.getBean(DeliverySettings.class).cities()).containsKeys("testpur", "pune");
            assertThat(normal.getBean(DeliverySettings.class).cities()).doesNotContainKey("testpur");
        }
    }

    @Configuration
    static class RoadDistances {
        @Bean
        DistanceCalculator roadDistance() {
            return (from, lat, lon) -> 42.0;
        }
    }

    @Test
    void aBeanOfYourOwnReplacesTheDefaultCalculator() {
        try (var ctx = new SpringApplicationBuilder(DeliveryApplication.class, RoadDistances.class).web(WebApplicationType.NONE).run()) {
            assertThat(ctx.getBeansOfType(DistanceCalculator.class)).containsOnlyKeys("roadDistance");
        }
    }

    @Test
    void straightLineDistanceMatchesAKnownOne() {
        DistanceCalculator d = new DistanceAutoConfiguration().straightLine();
        assertThat(d.km(new DeliverySettings.Location(18.5204, 73.8567), 19.0760, 72.8777)).isCloseTo(120.15, within(0.01));   // Pune to Mumbai
    }
}

package com.basketo.delivery;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.boot.webmvc.test.autoconfigure.AutoConfigureMockMvc;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.MockMvc;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.ResultActions;

import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.empty;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.get;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.post;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.content;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.jsonPath;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.status;

/** HTTP contract: a city's terms, checks the server works out itself, and every refusal. */
@SpringBootTest
@AutoConfigureMockMvc
class DeliveryContractTest {

    @Autowired
    MockMvc mvc;

    ResultActions check(String json) throws Exception {
        return mvc.perform(post("/delivery-checks").contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON).content(json));
    }

    @Test
    void aCitysTermsComeFromConfiguration() throws Exception {
        mvc.perform(get("/cities/Pune/delivery-terms"))
                .andExpect(status().isOk())
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.city").value("pune"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.radiusKm").value(6.0))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.feePaise").value(2500))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.minimumOrderPaise").value(14900));
    }

    @Test
    void anAddressInsideTheRadiusIsDeliverable() throws Exception {
        check("{\"city\":\"pune\",\"lat\":18.5362,\"lon\":73.8940,\"orderPaise\":25000}")   // Koregaon Park
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.distanceKm").value(4.94))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.deliverable").value(true))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.reasons", empty()));
    }

    @Test
    void theServerSaysTooFarAndTooSmallWhateverTheClientThinks() throws Exception {
        check("{\"city\":\"pune\",\"lat\":18.5913,\"lon\":73.7389,\"orderPaise\":9900}")      // Hinjewadi, Rs 99
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.distanceKm").value(13.28))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.deliverable").value(false))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.reasons[0]").value("OUT_OF_RANGE"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.reasons[1]").value("BELOW_MINIMUM"));
        check("{\"city\":\"pune\",\"lat\":18.5913,\"lon\":73.7389,\"orderPaise\":25000,\"distanceKm\":0}")
                .andExpect(status().isBadRequest());   // a client-side distance is not a field any more
    }

    @Test
    void aCityWeDoNotServeIs404() throws Exception {
        mvc.perform(get("/cities/jaipur/delivery-terms")).andExpect(status().isNotFound())
                .andExpect(content().contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_PROBLEM_JSON))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.title").value("City not served"));
        check("{\"city\":\"jaipur\",\"lat\":26.9,\"lon\":75.8,\"orderPaise\":25000}").andExpect(status().isNotFound());
    }

    @Test
    void badCoordinatesOrAmountsAre400() throws Exception {
        check("{\"city\":\"pune\",\"lat\":91,\"lon\":73.8,\"orderPaise\":25000}").andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
        check("{\"city\":\"pune\",\"lat\":18.5,\"lon\":73.8,\"orderPaise\":0}").andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
        check("{\"city\":\"pune\",\"lat\":18.5,\"lon\":73.8,\"orderPaise\":250.5}").andExpect(status().isBadRequest());

package com.basketo.delivery;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.AssertTrue;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.DecimalMax;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.DecimalMin;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Max;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Min;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotEmpty;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import org.springframework.boot.context.properties.ConfigurationProperties;
import org.springframework.validation.annotation.Validated;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * Per-city delivery settings from configuration (basketo.cities.*), checked when the app starts. A typo in a key,
 * a missing value or a minimum order of zero stops the app from starting, instead of quietly taking orders at Rs 0.
 * Wrapper types (Long, Double), not primitives: a missing value is null and fails @NotNull, never a silent 0.
 */
@ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "basketo", ignoreUnknownFields = false)
@Validated
record DeliverySettings(@NotEmpty Map<String, @Valid @NotNull City> cities) {

    record City(@NotNull @DecimalMin("0.5") @DecimalMax("15.0") Double radiusKm,
                @NotNull @Min(0) @Max(10_000) Long feePaise,
                @NotNull @Min(value = 9_900, message = "must be at least 9900 paise (Rs 99): a demo floor") Long minimumOrderPaise,
                @NotNull @Valid Location store,
                @Min(1) Long freeDeliveryAbovePaise,
                List<@Valid @NotNull FeeBand> feeBands) {

        /** Challenge 1: a rule across two fields. Checked by validation because the method starts with "is". */
        @AssertTrue(message = "free-delivery-above-paise must be above minimum-order-paise")
        public boolean isFreeDeliveryAboveMinimum() {
            return freeDeliveryAbovePaise == null || minimumOrderPaise == null || freeDeliveryAbovePaise > minimumOrderPaise;
        }

        /** Challenge 2: bands in increasing distance, the last one reaching the radius. */
        @AssertTrue(message = "fee-bands must increase and the last must reach radius-km")
        public boolean isFeeBandsCoverTheRadius() {
            if (feeBands == null || feeBands.isEmpty()) {
                return true;
            }
            for (int i = 1; i < feeBands.size(); i++) {
                if (feeBands.get(i).upToKm() <= feeBands.get(i - 1).upToKm()) {
                    return false;
                }
            }
            return radiusKm == null || feeBands.getLast().upToKm() >= radiusKm;
        }

        /** The fee for an order at this distance: banded if bands are set, free above the threshold. */
        long feeFor(double km, long orderPaise) {
            if (freeDeliveryAbovePaise != null && orderPaise >= freeDeliveryAbovePaise) {
                return 0;
            }
            if (feeBands == null || feeBands.isEmpty()) {
                return feePaise;
            }
            return feeBands.stream().filter(b -> km <= b.upToKm()).findFirst().orElse(feeBands.getLast()).feePaise();
        }
    }

    /** Challenge 2: one band, "up to this many km, this fee". */
    record FeeBand(@NotNull @DecimalMin("0.1") Double upToKm, @NotNull @Min(0) Long feePaise) {
    }

    record Location(@NotNull @DecimalMin("-90") @DecimalMax("90") Double lat, @NotNull @DecimalMin("-180") @DecimalMax("180") Double lon) {
    }
}

package com.basketo.delivery;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.DecimalMax;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.DecimalMin;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Min;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;

@RestController
class DeliveryController {

    record Terms(String city, double radiusKm, long feePaise, long minimumOrderPaise) {
    }

    /** No distance field: the client sends where the address is; the server works out how far it is. */
    record CheckRequest(@NotBlank String city, @NotNull @DecimalMin("-90") @DecimalMax("90") Double lat,
                        @NotNull @DecimalMin("-180") @DecimalMax("180") Double lon, @NotNull @Min(1) Long orderPaise) {
    }

    record Check(String city, double distanceKm, boolean deliverable, List<String> reasons, long feePaise,
                 long minimumOrderPaise, long orderPaise) {
    }

    private final DeliverySettings settings;
    private final DistanceCalculator distance;

    DeliveryController(DeliverySettings settings, DistanceCalculator distance) {
        this.settings = settings;
        this.distance = distance;
    }

    @GetMapping("/cities/{city}/delivery-terms")
    Terms terms(@PathVariable String city) {
        String key = city.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
        DeliverySettings.City c = find(key);
        return new Terms(key, c.radiusKm(), c.feePaise(), c.minimumOrderPaise());
    }

    @PostMapping("/delivery-checks")
    Check check(@Valid @RequestBody CheckRequest r) {
        String key = r.city().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
        DeliverySettings.City c = find(key);
        double km = distance.km(c.store(), r.lat(), r.lon());
        List<String> reasons = new ArrayList<>();
        if (km > c.radiusKm()) {
            reasons.add("OUT_OF_RANGE");
        }
        if (r.orderPaise() < c.minimumOrderPaise()) {
            reasons.add("BELOW_MINIMUM");
        }
        return new Check(key, Math.round(km * 100) / 100.0, reasons.isEmpty(), reasons, c.feeFor(km, r.orderPaise()),
                c.minimumOrderPaise(), r.orderPaise());
    }

    private DeliverySettings.City find(String city) {
        DeliverySettings.City c = settings.cities().get(city);
        if (c == null) {
            ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Basketo does not deliver in this city yet.");
            p.setTitle("City not served");
            throw new ErrorResponseException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, p, null);
        }
        return c;
    }
}

challenge/solution/DeliveryController.java

package com.basketo.delivery;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.DecimalMax;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.DecimalMin;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Min;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;

@RestController
class DeliveryController {

    record Terms(String city, double radiusKm, long feePaise, long minimumOrderPaise) {
    }

    /** No distance field: the client sends where the address is; the server works out how far it is. */
    record CheckRequest(@NotBlank String city, @NotNull @DecimalMin("-90") @DecimalMax("90") Double lat,
                        @NotNull @DecimalMin("-180") @DecimalMax("180") Double lon, @NotNull @Min(1) Long orderPaise) {
    }

    record Check(String city, double distanceKm, boolean deliverable, List<String> reasons, long feePaise,
                 long minimumOrderPaise, long orderPaise) {
    }

    private final DeliverySettings settings;
    private final DistanceCalculator distance;

    DeliveryController(DeliverySettings settings, DistanceCalculator distance) {
        this.settings = settings;
        this.distance = distance;
    }

    @GetMapping("/cities/{city}/delivery-terms")
    Terms terms(@PathVariable String city) {
        String key = city.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
        DeliverySettings.City c = find(key);
        return new Terms(key, c.radiusKm(), c.feePaise(), c.minimumOrderPaise());
    }

    @PostMapping("/delivery-checks")
    Check check(@Valid @RequestBody CheckRequest r) {
        String key = r.city().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
        DeliverySettings.City c = find(key);
        double km = distance.km(c.store(), r.lat(), r.lon());
        List<String> reasons = new ArrayList<>();
        if (km > c.radiusKm()) {
            reasons.add("OUT_OF_RANGE");
        }
        if (r.orderPaise() < c.minimumOrderPaise()) {
            reasons.add("BELOW_MINIMUM");
        }
        return new Check(key, Math.round(km * 100) / 100.0, reasons.isEmpty(), reasons, c.feeFor(km, r.orderPaise()),
                c.minimumOrderPaise(), r.orderPaise());
    }

    private DeliverySettings.City find(String city) {
        DeliverySettings.City c = settings.cities().get(city);
        if (c == null) {
            ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Basketo does not deliver in this city yet.");
            p.setTitle("City not served");
            throw new ErrorResponseException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, p, null);
        }
        return c;
    }
}

Short at Foundations: the choices that matter here.

Implementation approach

  1. Write the trap test: the old settings start with a typo and a zero minimum.
  2. Write the settings as records with wrapper types and constraints; refuse unknown keys.
  3. Test startup failures in small contexts; test profiles and environment overrides on the real app.
  4. Move the distance into the server, behind a replaceable default.

Database design

None in this station. If settings move to a table: city_delivery_terms with check constraints mirroring the record's (radius between 0.5 and 15, minimum at least 9900), so a bad row is refused by the database too.

A Foundations station: the considerations to know, no runbook.

Deployments
A bad setting now fails the deployment's startup, so the old version keeps serving. That is the point: the error reaches an engineer, not a customer.
Secrets and environments
Per-environment values come from environment variables or a secret store, never committed. Profiles hold whole sets of differences (dev, staging).
Trust
Anything the client could change (distance, price, discount) is computed or looked up on the server.
Distance
Straight-line distance is always shorter than the road. A real radius check may use a routing service, plugged in as its own DistanceCalculator.

Answers are hidden until opened, so the learner tries first.

Interview takeaways

How do you make Spring Boot configuration fail fast?

Bind it into a @ConfigurationProperties class or record, add @Validated with Bean Validation constraints, use wrapper types so missing values are null, and set ignoreUnknownFields = false so typos are errors.

How does an environment variable override a property?

Relaxed binding: upper case, dots to underscores, dashes removed. basketo.cities.pune.fee-paise becomes BASKETO_CITIES_PUNE_FEEPAISE, and it wins over application.yaml.

What is a profile?

A named set of configuration (application-dev.yaml) applied on top of the defaults when the profile is active.

What is auto-configuration?

Configuration classes Spring Boot applies after your own beans, usually with conditions like @ConditionalOnMissingBean, so they supply sensible defaults you can replace by defining your own bean.

Why compute the distance on the server?

The client controls everything it sends. A value that decides price or eligibility must come from data the server trusts.
